To: @marco
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Desert Palms codes and pinning tray

Marco,

I’m pissed that I’m dealing with this again. Yvette needs three copies for 9B today, and there’s nothing in the code sheet to cut from. You told me Desert Palms was done and the keys were with Yvette, but the codes aren’t there. And your pinning tray is still sitting on the counter in their leasing office.

I told everybody in August: every rekey, every master job, codes go in the sheet the same day, before you leave the van. Address, unit, code. No exceptions. I told you the same thing after Kessler in September. This isn’t new, and it isn’t optional. When the codes don’t get logged, somebody else is left scrambling, and now Yvette and that tenant are waiting on us.

Go back to Desert Palms today. Decode 9B at a minimum so we can get those copies cut. If you can get all 14 units decoded, do that too, and put every code in the sheet before you leave. Don’t just text me the codes or tell me you’ll get to it later. Make sure the address and unit are clear in the sheet so we can use it.

Bring the pinning tray back to the shop while you’re there. It shouldn’t have been left at the leasing office.

I’m not looking to fire you. You’re good with your hands and I value the work you do. But this has happened before, I’ve already addressed it, and I need to know I can count on you to finish the job properly. Let me know when 9B is decoded, the codes are logged, and you’ve got the tray back. From here on out, same-day logging needs to happen every time.
